rv.q: I don’t think I have ever seen another play that was so tonally jarring in such a calculated and effective manner.
The Last Living Gun is worth their efforts.
It’s a smart, feisty show, and Roseen’s direction and the cast keep a firm hand on the shifting tonal elements in Stevens’s intriguing tale.

cn.t: This allegorical Western fantasy about hunting the world's last gun rewards patient viewers with a clever, cross-genre journey that overcomes its rough-around-the-edges production values to deliver an engaging theatrical experience.
